issues.issue: What standard of review applies to the Federal Court judge's review of the Delegate's opinion?
issues.result_quote: I conclude that Justice Kelen applied the proper standard of review to the questions of law raised in this application for judicial review, i.e. correctness.

issues.issue: Must the Delegate assess the nature and severity of acts under s.115(2)(b) when there is no risk on return (certified question 1)?
issues.applicant_position: Says Kelen erred: the nature and severity of acts must still be assessed even where there is no risk of return.
issues.respondent_position: Agrees with the appellant that Kelen erred on this point (para 38).
issues.result_quote: I propose to answer “no” to the first certified question as the Delegate failed to follow the steps suggested above in forming his opinion.

issues.issue: What standard of proof applies to a s.115(2)(b) opinion?
issues.result_quote: I therefore conclude that the proper standard for a determination under subsection 115(2) of the Act is reasonable grounds.

issues.issue: Whose acts count under s.115(2)(b) (personal acts, or the gang's acts through complicity), and what complicity test applies?
issues.result_quote: there must be reasonable grounds to believe that the person committed, himself or through complicity, as defined in our criminal legal system, acts of organized criminality.

issues.issue: What threshold must the nature and severity of acts meet to justify removal?
issues.applicant_position: Says the non-refoulement principle sets a high threshold for the exceptions, so only grave conduct qualifies.
issues.result_quote: Thus, only acts which are of substantial gravity will meet this high threshold.

issues.issue: Did the Delegate properly link the appellant to the gang's acts and reach a complicity finding?
issues.applicant_position: Says the opinion rests on the gang's acts without a reasoned personal link to him.
issues.result_quote: it falls short of meeting the personalized fact-driven inquiry dictated by paragraph 115(2)(b) of the same Act.

issues.issue: Should the Court order the Minister to help him return to Canada while his case is reconsidered?
issues.applicant_position: Asks the Court to compel the Minister to help him return urgently so he can remain in Canada while reconsidered.
issues.result_quote: The record indicates no special circumstances for this Court to compel the Minister to act in a particular fashion.
